title: Haav Pi
description: Raspberry Pi drill-down: power/firmware, CPU, memory, SD card, network/LTE, logs. Source: haav-telemetry/dashboards/pi.json (generated).

panels.title: Scrape time
panels.description: How long Alloy's node_exporter takes to collect. Slow = Pi overloaded or a hung /sys read.

panels.title: pi-health script
panels.description: Red if haav-pi-health.timer stopped or its textfile is unparseable.

panels.title: Processes running
panels.description: Runnable tasks (includes the collectors themselves; ~5-7 is normal idle). Sustained double digits = contention.

panels.title: Reboots in range
panels.description: Boot-time changes in the selected range (brownouts, kill switch, battery swaps).

panels.title: Throttle flags: now
panels.description: vcgencmd get_throttled bits 0-3: active this second.

panels.title: Throttle flags: since boot
panels.description: vcgencmd get_throttled bits 16-19: happened at any point since boot (latched until reboot).

panels.title: Raw get_throttled
panels.description: Bits 0-3 now, 16-19 since boot. 0x50000 = under-voltage + throttled earlier.

panels.title: Temperature vs ARM clock
panels.description: Clock drops while temp is high = thermal throttling. Clock drops with normal temp = under-voltage or just idle (ondemand governor).

panels.title: Core voltage
panels.description: SoC core rail set by the firmware's DVFS. Rises with clock; sudden dips alongside under-voltage point at the 5 V supply.

panels.title: Under-voltage (now vs since boot)
panels.description: 'since boot' stepping to 1 while 'now' blips = a brief sag, e.g. motors spinning up on a shared 5 V converter.

panels.title: Per-core usage
panels.description: One pegged core with the rest idle = a single-threaded process spinning (e.g. a stuck collector).

panels.title: CPU by mode
panels.description: Share of all cores. iowait = waiting on the SD card.

panels.title: Load vs cores
panels.description: Load above the dashed line = work queuing. On a Pi, load also counts tasks stuck in uninterruptible SD I/O.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: 'used' creeping up over hours with no restart = a leak (haav-mavlink, haavd).

panels.title: Time until full
panels.description: Free space ÷ how fast it shrank over the last 6 h. Reads low for a few hours after an apt install/update; trust it when it stays low (runaway logs or WAL).

panels.title: Read-only
panels.description: Kernel remounts / read-only after card errors (common after sudden power loss).

panels.title: SD throughput (read up, write down)
panels.description: Needs the diskstats collector (added to config.alloy 2026-11-23).

panels.title: SD busy & IOPS
panels.description: Busy near 100% with low throughput = the card is struggling (worn or failing). Best early warning before it goes read-only.

panels.title: Written in range
panels.description: SD wear indicator. Journald + Alloy WAL are the main writers.

panels.title: Throughput per interface (rx up, tx down)
Link state per interface
panels.description: Kernel operstate (netclass collector). wwan0 flapping = LTE dropping; tailscale0 down = no SSH.

panels.title: Errors & drops per interface
panels.description: Should be flat zero. Sustained errors on wwan0 = poor signal or USB power trouble on the modem.

panels.title: LTE daily burn rate
panels.description: Bytes/day if the last hour's wwan0 rate held. Lines: 10 and 20 MB/hr budget (240 / 480 MB/day).

panels.title: Days to burn the 500 MB SIM
panels.description: 500 MB ÷ current daily rate: run-time budget for a fresh SIM, not what's left on yours (1NCE portal has that).

panels.title: Sample lag (data freshness)
panels.description: Age of the newest sample at each point. Saw-tooth up to 15 s is normal; climbs then gaps when LTE drops; holes fill in once the WAL replays.
